title: Started Valtrex, then on to Naltrexone  -- should I not get my hopes up?
body:
Hi there,
As I've mentioned before, I'm being treated at the Stanford Chronic Fatigue clinic. Last week, reviewing my blood tests, they said first they want to treat my elevated EBV (ebv ab vca, igg 370.0  0.0-17.9 U/mL). I only tested high for the IgG antibody.
It's disheartening to hear that a lot of people think EBV is not relevant to CFS.
Apparently at Stanford they think it's worth trying to address it.
So I'm taking Valtrex for two weeks and then we'll assess how I feel, and perhaps I will continue. And then at that point, I'm supposed to start taking Naltrexone.
Anyone have luck on Naltrexone?
thanks,
Laura

comments.body:
There are many threads on Low Dose Naltrexone. You can find them with a
Google Site Search
. Good luck with this!

if you haven't started valtex I suggest you start very slowly. Same thing with LDN.
Read
@Mary
recent post about her LDN experience.

I think EBV is VERY relevant.  I am on a different protocol for EBV and am seeing improvement.     If for some reason the Valtrex doesn't work for you (I hope that it does) I would be glad to share what I'm taking for this beast.

I have no idea what my EBV titers are, my illness did start with Mono, I have been on LDN since 2009, so about 6 years now
GG
I  think  you may need more than  2 weeks on valtrex to notice a good  effect??
Yes, I think the idea is I would go three months, maybe up to a year.

I don't discount treating viruses in CFS. My own experience is that Valtrex has been a very useful drug for me so far. I am not able to pay for the dose my private doctor would like me to take however or the other drugs he would like me to try.
I'd love to be in your position of being seen at Stanford and being able to be tested and treated in the way they are doing.
I had no bad reaction to Vatrex, found that it did nothing in small doses once a day or spread over a day and only at 1gm a day at once get the good effects.
Never tried LDN but it is on my list for some day when I can afford it.

It took years of illness before getting to Stanford. I have an HMO and luckily Stanford is now in my doctor's group. However, I can't use their lab, because my insurance doesn't allow it. Still, I feel lucky. Not holding my breath that it'll work, though.
Yes, at two weeks we were going to see how I'm tolerating it. Then if I'm doing okay we're supposed to add LDN.

I would say that the simple fact that you are now under the care of some excellent ME/CFS specialists is reason to have hope.
I would also say that expectation of very rapid large improvement (on the scale of weeks) or expectation of a complete cure or remission might be overly optimistic.
My daughter and I both take Valtrex and LDN, among a number of other things, and have had a great deal of improvement.  It did not happen overnight and we are not cured, although my daughter appears to be in remission.  I am pretty far from remission so far, but am very glad for the improvement I got as a result of good treatment from ME/CFS specialists.

Mary, do you feel perhaps that you took too much LDN initially? Also tiredness and spacey is common at the beginning. Im not sure about depression.
You know your body but I wonder if you tried again (when you are strong enough) with a tiny amount and stuck with that tiny amount for a month it might get better.
Im sure you've thought all this.
I wouldn't endure depression under any circumstances so completely understand your stance.
What a shame.
x

Piping in about LDN - I've been taking it since 2012 and consider it extremely helpful in improving sleep, mood, and energy. Heeding advice on this site, I started low, at 0.2 mg (even at that dose I had unpleasant side effects of insomnia and headache for 2 weeks) and worked my way up to 1.5 mg by increasing a couple of mg each week.  Over the next 2 years I worked up to 4.5 mg in a divided dose (3 mg at bedtime, 1.5 mg in the morning).  I'm grateful that I can tolerate it and hope never to be without it.
Since I had an adverse reaction to valtrex, the doc now wants to give me famciclovir. Have you tried that?

Yep so far naltrexone works wonders for me.  I have hobbies again,  I'm exercising more. My brain fog is mostly gone. Now when I crash I can usually still play video games or enjoy TV rather than just lieing on the couch doing nothing.   I feel like I'm euphoric most days now
It helps energy,  but only so much. My other medications work better now with LDN (kratom,  Marijuana,  ritalin) .
It helps libido immensely.  When I first noticed the effect I pretty much just masterbate on the couch a few days straight (i know TMI! But it just feels good to actually be able to do stuff again!!) . Since I have returned to romancing the ladies and have had a couple dates so far
It's really nice,  mostly I feel like a normal person who fatigues easily now. Fatigue and crashing are about the only 2 things I have to worry about now. Hell even when I crash I am still able to exercise most of the time now!

Oh Lord what Id give for some euphoria.
I HATE that I couldnt tolerate LDN. It was my biggest hope.
Glad others are feeling better though.
I might try an even smaller  dose than 0.1mg in the future. Seems ridiculous but perhaps I only need a tiny amount.
My specialist told me at least 6 months taking 1g. @ 3x/ day, up to 1 year.

title: starting LDN. Does it work?
body:
Haven't been on the forums in a while but I'm back
I'm thinking of stating LDN very soon. I'm going to the gp next week with an info paper about it and ask if he can do a prescription out of his budget. If not then I will ask him to write a permission form saying that I'm okay to have the prescription. Then I will contact a consultation company (e-med. Any opinions on them? Other websites don't seem to have as much info but their website seems a little... backwards? E-med.co.uk)
Has anyone had any success with it? Most of the testimonials seem to be for MS and not ME. Also what sort of side affects are involved for cfs patients. I don't have drug sensitivities luckily but I do want to know if anyone had side affects.

comments.body:
There are several threads on LDN and the effects, side-effects, and non-effects that ME patients have had. But the search engine at the top doesn't handle 3 letter searches, so click on forums at the top, scroll down to resources and click on google site search. Here you should find plenty of comments.
Just off-hand, it seems to help about 50% of patients, but you need to start with a very low dose (.5 mg for some) and take a long time (months) to work up to a full 4 mg dose.
I am one of the ones it has helped.
Best,
Sushi

I started in .25 Mgs a few weeks ago.  I started at .5 Mgs and had a horrible headache but that went away at the lower dose.
I immediately felt better. But it completely screwed up my sleep so I stopped it.  That is a known side effect, one of the only one I'm aware of.
I am going to try again in the morning as soon as I get my Famvir on board.
I have a friend who swears by it.  If you can get it try it. Start at a low dose and work up.

@
minkeygirl
down I need to buy special measuring apparatus for it? Those doses a very low and the most I have is a 2.5ml medicine spoon.
@
Sushi
thank you.

@
Ambrosia_angel
I had mine compounded so it was easier for me.   One thing you might want to try is using water.   Here is the basics of how it works.
Take 100 ml water in cup.  Add 100 mgs of naltrexone.  Stir and then use a syringe to draw 1cc for 1 mg.   Make sense?  Less  mixture for a smaller dose.  It probably tastes like crap but you can wash it down with something else.   (I was able to get 60 ml syringes from a veterinarian or on ebay.   You can get much smaller ones online also.)   Or take 25 ml water and 25 mgs of naltrexone.
There are some threads here on how to do that and how to store the rest of the liquid, which I think was in a sealed container in the refrigerator.
I planned on started with .5 mgs but because I had such a bad headache I split the capsules.  So maybe try that to start.
You can PM me if you need better instructions on how to do that water method.
Also, if you cant get a doc to get it for you there are places you can get it for pretty cheap without an RX.

@
Ambrosia_angel
What form of LDN do you have or hope to get? Sometimes it comes in liquid and sometimes as a tablet or capsule. In each case you have to look at the dilution and measure out your dose--unless you have capsules that are the exact dose you need.
I measure my liquid LDN with an insulin syringe with the needle removed.
Sushi

I understand. I have to dilute it by 1:1 then take out (e.g.) 1ml which will be 0.5ml of naltrexone. Maybe I'll get a pipette too.
I'm reading people's stories on here and a lot seem to have negative experiences with it. It's making me feeling a bit weary of it now :/ feeling a bit deflated before I've tried.
Also does the increased endorphins have an anti depressant effect to it? I'd like to avoid that tbh. I don't want anything messing with my current thought process. Especially if I have to come of it suddenly.

My guess is that most of the negative reactions are from starting with too high a dose. Though it is true that it is very common to get insomnia at first--for me for a few days every time I raised the dose. But when I got to 3 mgs my sleep became much better and has stayed that way.
I take it at bedtime so the increased endorphins happen during sleep--I don't notice a thing from that.
Sushi

title: Starting LDN - Morning Agitation
body:
Hi, I'm needing input from people who have taken LDN.
I started on 1.5 mg two nights ago, and both mornings I've experienced agitation and been upset. This is drastically different from my usual morning state, which is draggy and groggy.
Have other people experienced this? And does it go away? And would it be worth a try to take it a couple hours earlier in the evening (say, 8:30 instead of 10:30)?
I
am
drowning in red tape these days and overwhelmed, but that's been true for 3-4 weeks.

comments.body:
Maybe you started with too high a dose?  I started much lower .5 and
@Sushi
started at .25 if I remember right.
It says to take between 9 and 3 am I think. Can't quite remember.

Some people are very sensitive to the dose. I actually started at 1.5 mg and took it at night. I didn't have morning agitation but we all seem to respond differently. I did titrate my dose up very slowly--it took 4 months to reach 4.5 mgs.

Interesting, I was wondering about the dose. My ND started me at the "lowest" dose because of Hashi's, and having to keep a close watch on thyroid meds.
So does it work OK to open a capsule and take half of it? (All the money I could save, haha.)

Sure! Personally I crush a 50 mg tablet (generic from an ordinary pharmacy), mix it with 50 mls of distilled water and keep in the fridge, measuring out my dose with an oral syringe. This costs about $1.50 per month after insurance pays its share.

I'm definitely getting the insomnia, too, around 3 or 4 am. And getting up to pee 4-5 times a night instead of my usual 3 times (groan!).
What does the endorphin rush feel like?
Mental feel-good. I had this the next day after my first dose.

The endorphin rush to me feels euphoric, mental feel-good like Sushi mentioned.
Have you ever experienced a runners high? (pre-onset of your illness ofcourse!) It kinda feels like that.
Yes, it was a hiker's high. Often, and at altitude!

I started using match-head size doses, increased by that much over several days (from a 3mg capsule) Even this tiny amount affected my sleep and provoked detox response. Thankfully the negative effects passed quickly. good luck w/ this.
FWIW, I take mine first thing in the morning. That seems to work the best for me!

Update: I'm still taking just 0.75 mg each night. My morning energy has improved noticeably!
Instead of just dragging myself around barely coping with the basics (food, getting dressed, taking & tracking supplements), I'm managing to get a little bit done most mornings -- whether it's dishes or red tape (which I've been swimming in).

I just poped in here to leave a response in the general LDN post but saw yours.   I am having anger managment problems on LDN!  I started the first of november and settled on 2ml until I see a reduction in anger.
Last night I woke up and my husband was snoring.  I was awake for 3 hours and was so angry that I was considering divorce!!!
I'm not sure if this is related but on steroids I have roidrage.  Not sure if my body is shifting to make more chemicals. IDK...  I also have massive food cravings.  Worse  than when pregnant.  Other than that I don't have any other side effects.

Anger + insomnia. That sounds like the LDN. Not that I know anything about dosing, but how many milligrams are in your 2 ml dose?
I'm such a light sleeper and my DH & I both thrash around a bit, so the separate rooms option works well for us. He needs good sleep as much as I do.

I'm having regular morning exhaustion again now, and tried taking a whole cap (1.5 mg) a few nights ago, but it didn't do anything noticeable for me. Guess I will try it again.
I'm having more histamine-type symptoms: balloon-type bloating after many foods, and lots of hot flushes (but not a high temp -- it's usually around 98.2 F / 36.7 C. I say "flushes" because my face turns pink.
Can this be related to LDN or its effect on thyroid?
switch to AM dosing. Less problems.

title: Starting LDN tonight, any suggestions?
body:
I think it was in 2007, a doctor started me on LDN.  I knew very little about it and he should have known better, but he started me off on 4 mgs right off the bat. Needless to say I didn't sleep and never went back to it.
Now I have .5 mgs and I'll stay with that for 2 weeks and then go again in 2 more weeks.   I've been through a bad spell with sleep lately and I'm not looking forward to the possibility of not sleeping again.  I've read some people here said they went really slowly and took a long time to get to the full dose they can tolerate so I'm wondering if I should have gotten .25 mgs.  But if I have to I can always open these and do it that way.
I know I have to take it at night. Can someone tell me when, with food?  I turn off the lights at 10 pm.
Thanks for the help.

comments.body:
We are all different, but I have the  best results taking it in the morning. I have been on it for over three years now, and still limit my dose to 1.5 mg.
I would suggest taking your dose every other day for a week or so to see how it goes. LDN has never helped my sleep much, in fact it keeps me awake, and that is why I take it mornings. It is quite possible that I am not taking a large enough dose to help with sleep, but the 1.5 mg dose seems to help a little, and any higher dose makes me feel worse, so I don't push it.
I needed to back off the dose when I started to .2 mg every other day. I very slowly worked my way up to where I am today over the course of several months. It is amazing to me that the normal dose of Naltrexone is 50 mg. To me, that dose sounds lethal! I have found that you can't force it, that the best approach is to start very slowly, and work your way up to a dose that you can handle.
I realize that that is not much of an answer, but the dosage really needs to be determined by each individual user, and what works for one won't work for the next.
John

jstefl

GG

I did some reading and you want to take it during one of the two endorphin peaks so it works better.  ( don't ask me to repeat the science)  The better one is at night.
I think I'm going to suck it up and take it at 9 tonight and hope whatever happens happens early enough so that I can get to sleep.   If not it only stays in you for 4 hours.
Some said they liked the hallucinations from the endorphin rush.  We shall see. I just know I'd rather feel like crap if I've had some sleep then not sleep and feel even worse.
.375 mg was too much for me. I suggest you try .25 mg.

title: Starting Low Dose Naltrexone treatment on methylation protocol?
body:
Hey all,
As some of you may recall I'm having a HORRIBLE time with inflammation, allergies and food sensitivities. Looking into inflammation more lead me to discovering LDN (Low Dose Naltrexone) which is showing a lot of promise in autoimmune conditions. It also seems to be pretty well tolerated and safe. I'd really like to try it.
Is anyone here familiar with it and know of any reason to be concerned about doing it in conjunction with Fredd's protocol?
Thanks so much!
Audrey

comments.body: Start low and work yourself up slowly to the full dosage, which is usually 4.5 milligrams. You will most likely have some sleep disturbance and realistic dreaming when you start. This will diminish with time. It can be lessened or eliminated by taking the LDN in the morning instead of the evening. LDN is usually taken at night, but does not have to be. Also, as with other treatments, it can increase or exacerbate inflammation or symptoms in the beginning. That's why I say start low and increase slowly. Of course, there are those that are able to jump right in to the full dosage and have little to no side effects. I don't know of any reason you can't use in conjunction with a methylation protocol. Hope this helps and good luck.
Thanks Drex! I'm getting the subscription filled today. I'll report back in a bit.
Hope it worked (works) good for you, chil. And, yes, i also wanna know if i can use LDN along with the b12 treatment protocol.

And though the usual starting dose is 1.5 mg, a number of patients here have found that this is too much and have started with .5 mg. One reason to take it during the night is that when your opiate receptors are blocked you can feel a bit depressed. If you take it at night you sleep through the few hours where they are blocked. But then you might have trouble with sleep the first few days on each higher dose.
I and others have also found that raising the dose
really
slowly is important so that you don't suddenly awaken you immune system and get a lot of side-effects from it attacking things. It took me about 4 months to get up to dose.
Best wishes with this. I hope it helps you.
Sushi

Id even go as far to say that
1. Always started at .5mgs especially if you expect to try taking it everyday

title: Starting Mestinon treatment first week in January - any advice?
body: I'm starting Mestinon treatment in a couple of days. I'm very sensitive to medication and would like some advice concerning starting dosage from other members with experience form Mestinon. My doctor don't have any experience with this treatment, so any advice would be highly appreciated

comments.body:
I'm thinking of giving it a go too. This is what I was advised as I am sensitive to meds too
* Start with 1/4 tab (15 mg) once a day
* Increase by 1/4 tab every 7 days as tolerated.
* 1/4 tab two times a day
* 1/2 tab in am and 1/4 tab in pm
* 1/2 tab in am and 1/2 tab in pm
* continue to increase in this fashion up to 60 mg two times a day based on effects/side effects
* Monitor BP and hr
Half life is very short, if it doesn't jive with you... it's over in about 4-5 hours.
Be aware that nausea can be a side effect.

Thanks
@wigglethemouse
Just to be clear :
You mean to take 15 mg once a day for 7 days, and then increase to 15 mg x 2 times daily for 7 days, and then increase to 30 mg morning and 15 mg in the evening and so on…………………?

The doctor will give me antidote if needed
. Hope I won't need it
I can live with that! 'm very sick at the moment, so nausea is "nothing" at the moment!
That's right. Proceed as tolerated.

I think it's a good idea to start on a low dose, stay on that does for a while, then slowly increase the dose, wait another while, and then repeat.  Sometimes I didn't experience common side effects on increasing the dose (nausea, aches), and sometimes I did.  Those side effects went away after a few days to a week, so stick with it if you can.
I actually started on a somewhat higher dose--I started off at 30mg 3x per day.  I stayed on that dose for one month, and then went up to 60 mg 3x per day.  After another month I was put on an extended release capsule of 180 mg just once per day.
In the end I had unpleasant side effects from Mestinon that weren't listed: chills, breathlessness, and constipation.  These made me miserable enough that I stopped taking the pills and was put on something else.  I wonder if I might have tolerated the medicine better if I had started off slower as
@wigglethemouse
suggested.  But even though I had to stop I'm glad I at least tried it.
One big tip: I kept my bottle of pills on a post-it note with little boxes for AM, noon, and PM, and I checked off the boxes as I took each pill.  That way, I could easily see whether or not I had taken my pill (I'm pretty forgetful), so that helped me keep on track with the routine.  I also put daily alarms on my phone to remind me to take the pills.

Oh, I almost forgot to add: you'll be on such a low dose at first that you shouldn't notice much of a difference in your energy level.
If you do start to feel better as the dosage slowly increases, don't increase your activity level too much.  Sometimes when people start to feel better, they go a little crazy, overdo it, and then crash.

Yes, start off very slowly
Yes: My main advice is to be very careful not do too much physical activity while you are feeling good.

I'm like you, thinking of starting in January. I don't know the answer to that. You can look at some prescription drug websites such as this that quotes
https://www.rxlist.com/mestinon-drug.htm

I had my first two small doses today. First a 5 mg dose at 10 am and a new dose at 13 pm (gave me an effective dose of 7-8 mg at 14.30 pm as a result of the half-life of the first pill).

Me feet (especially my toes) changed color from blue to a more normal skin color (my toes changed to light red). I felt calmer, almost like the “sympathetic storm” went from a storm to light breeze. After a couple of hour “the storm” and my blue feet was back

Yes I do have a new life!
but still need to be careful not to do too much because I still get PEM (but much milder than in the past).
When I take 30mg mestinon every four hours, I can now do things out of bed for four or five hours, as long as I pace carefully.
I did three hours of light gardening this morning.

I started with very small doses (5 mg x 2 daily) and increased very slow. I’m now on 4 x 10 mg and are still tolerating Mestinone   I expect I have to increase the dosage to 4 x 30 mg before I see any big changes in my health (this will take me weeks / months).
My doctor observed me the first 2 hours after I took the first pill and he had an antidote ready in case of any reaction (the antidote was atropin). I don’t think this was necessary but I  have reacted to different drugs so my doctor is extremely careful

title: Support with pyridostigmine and midodrine
body:
Will try to keep this succinct, but my partner has been seeing some benefits from taking pyridostigmine with midodrine the past week but we're having difficulty with the dosing, and figuring out what mechanisms are affecting what symptoms.
They had tried both medicines previously in isolation and found both just worsened their symptoms, but they seem to be working better in combination and we think we understand why.
The pyridostigmine is massively improving their muscle weakness and general nerve function- their nerves had been constantly either overstimulated or under functioning, we think likely due to chronic hypoperfusion and small fibre neuropathy, the latter being either from ongoing or previous inflammation and immune activity. But, the pyridostigmine has a big impact on vagus nerve and increases parasympathetic activity, and vadodilation. Where their body has been essentially running on increased sympathetic tone and activity, with this reduced it seems to worsen blood flow and oxygen perfusion.
The midodrine has helped counteract this by increasing vasoconstriction. Alone midodrine increased sympathetic activity way too much, and that increased the constriction to a point of worsening blood flow.
So it has been a real challenge figuring out the right ratio, timing and dose of both. The added challenge is that too much pyridostigmine, increases acetylcholine levels to a point that worsens muscle weakness. And as it has been helping nerve function, and their body is maintaining acetylcholine levels itself, the cutoff for too much pyridostigmine is lowering literally day by day. In a week they've gone from 30mg 3x a day to 10mg 3x a day. It will be perfect for a day, or morning, then seem to hit that top level where it overshoots and we have to lower it again. Which then means midodrine has to be reduced to match. (BP has often not been too relevant to general oxygen perfusion and blood flow, we can often tell more by how much their veins bulge, peripheral temperature, feelings of tightness, etc.)
We are scared that we won't be able to get this right, to where they can just take the same dose every day. There are also other factors that are not being helped. Their energy can still get really bad, we think metabolic dysfunction or still not good enough oxygen perfusion. Their cognitive ability isn't improving at all, the capacity to do anything with the strength pyridostigmine gives them.
Their specialist is also wanting to do some high dose steroids, which we had asked for before trying this, because it really seemed like truing to sort immune function must be the way. But with this maybe helping, we don't know if we want to delay that or still go ahead.
Does anyone have any experience with the above, or can offer some advice?
Any thoughts on why within a day or less can a dose go from being perfect, to being too much? How is their body maintaining acetylcholine levels that quickly?
Also any thoughts on what we could do about their energy and cognitive function? Would adding something like fludrocortisone also help improve oxygen perfusion?
This is just a nightmare trying to get right, I feel like we need to speak to a doctor once or twice a day to help with this, not just one phonecall every few months.
Any thoughts on acetylcholine, oxygen perfusion, neuropathy, severe autonomic dysfunction, etc, appreciated.

comments.body:
I don’t have the expertise to help you, but wondering if you have already tried searching PR for threads with titles of the two drugs your partner is taking?
I know there has been a lot of discussion on PR about “mestinon” or “pyridostigmine” and probably separate threads in “midodrine”.
As always, best wishes to you and your partner.

I'm on this exact combo of meds and it's the only meds that have made a noticeable difference in my illness.
I'm not sure how much mestinon is or isn't contributing. I have taken the max dose before without noticing much but I've been on a much lower dose 60-120mg since starting midodrine. Haven't really tried Mido without it so don't know about that.
I think one of the benefits of midodrine itself is lowering the sympathetic response in the brain. I look at it this way, if there is some sort of vascular issue the brain might compensate by releasing a load of adrenaline to help blood flow. It does help the blood flow issue but now your brain is swimming in norepinephrine.
Taking midodrine provides the same band aid to the blood flow issue meaning the brain no longer needs to produce quite so much noradrenaline.
I don't have PEM but I do have post viral POTS and what I call chronic bounding pulse. I have noticed the midodrine reduces the heavy pulse and also allows my brain to be a little more calmer. It also has significantly improved my sleep quality.
As far as dosing goes I have read that some people find they no longer have to take midodrine after a while and it essentially cured their POTS. Maybe if the brain isn't producing noradrenaline all the time it allows the body to heal or maybe stops disrupting the immune system.
It's a tricky situation but just try playing it by ear and judging day by day how much you think you might need. Tolerance shouldn't be an issue though I have found one or two people on reddit claiming they became tolerant.
Is your partner sitting up when they take it?
For me the mestinon barely feels like its doing anything even at really high doses. I wonder if this points to peripheral neuropathy.

Thanks for your reply, good to hear from someone on the same combo, also seeing a benefit. Nothing else has consistently helped like this has.
Agree with this, where their body has been so reliant on sympathetic over activity just to function, midodrine is taking some of that responsibility. But unfortunately its like, their body has been so dysfunctional for so long, there are still just such enormous swings happening as various systems try to compensate. Mestinon has been increasing the strength of nerve signals, but that also seems to have amped up their sympathetic nerve signals too, so they're getting lots of the symptoms we usually see when that's on overdrive- panic, shaking, a bad bad feeling of no energy, poor sleep. When the mestinon is working at its best, even with midodrine I think their sympathetic tone is still so high, that its still overreacting.
They're also quite badly getting this feeling of low oxygen perfusion. Pale lips and skin, lightheadedness, shortness of breath. Even if BP and pulse oxygen are reading OK. So even if the vasoconstriction of the midodrine is balancing the vasodilation of the mestinon, there's still not good perfusion. Wondering if fludrocortisone is needed to also bring up the blood volume.
And their energy is worsening a lot, they're really scared about the impact on their ME. They can stand and walk thanks to the mestinon. But there's this hollow feeling of no energy, limiting their capacity to do anything but move their muscles. May be from poor oxygen perfusion still. Or maybe more likely is if their nerves are functioning so much better than they have in literal years, their body is not used to keeping up with that level of nerve activity. I don't want to just, wait and hope their body catches up and starts meeting the demand though. I just don't know what to do to mitigate these secondary effects of mestinon working so well.

When I was at my worst a year ago I'd get this at night fairly often. My heart rate would be high and my heart pounding HARD but I'd feel sort of light headed, like blood was drained out of my brain, and almost like I was dying despite laying down. One time I even wrote down my passwords and things on a bit of paper for my brother to find in-case I didn't make it through the night.
I think it happening in the night was probably due to less sympathetic causing less perfusion, but I was lying down and my HR and pulse force was elevated. What was causing the lack of perfusion?
I think in that case it was B12 deficiency as I came out of the worst of it when I started B12 injections last year.
The weird thing is, my diet has been repleat in b12 for all the time since I've been ill. Also I had taken B12 supplements in various forms (including transdermal oils) without noticing benefit. All I can think is something is interfering with B12 absorption in my gut.
Anyway the point is, the b12 was probably causing some sort of pseudo anemia exaserbating my blood flow / nutrient exchange issues. Well people with post viral illness have probably got something else causing the same type of problem.
Is it low blood volume, blood pooling, excess vasodilation, poor nutrient exchange (mito dysfunction, thick cell membranes)?
I have no idea myself, just sort of experimenting with doses and trying to figure out what works.
Hopefully they'll start to recondition so to speak and you'll reach a stable point. Just got to keep messing around with the doses.
When I did my first methyl B12 injection last may for days after I thought I'm never doing that again, my POTS became much worse, but when that settled I noticed my baseline had improved a little.

We've often thought about it the opposite way, that during the day engaging their nervous system and nerves actually help them regulate to a degree, but when they lay down to sleep, everything become dysregulated, and its like their nerves are screaming, but then there's also possibly not good enough perfusion at the same time.
That's interesting the injections helped you when the oral supplements didn't, possibly is a bypassing of some dysfunctional part of the metabolism of digestion. We have also found they have a bad reaction to injesting basically anything, we think where there is some initial automatic nervous system response that kicks in when consuming something, and then their sympathetic nervous system kicks in to try and compensate for all the blood pooling in their digestion, maybe.
I really hope so, but it seems like the more the pyridostigmine is strengthening and helping their nerves, the stronger the sympathetic response is getting too. And their energy concerning actual capacity to do any activity is lessening. We are really struggling to keep things stable, even as we are tracking patterns and arcs more.

@SpinachHands
Maybe B12 injections would be worth a shot just to rule it out. They are relatively cheap and shouldn't cause too much side effects (methylB12 could cause overmethylation, hyroxyB12 shouldn't). I did feel worse for a couple days after the first methylB12 injection.
I get similar things when consuming anything, even just water. I think it's the blood pooling in the gut like you say. Maybe food also stimulates parasympathetic to which our bodies respond with a stronger sympathetic to maintain vasoconstriction.
It's a real tricky situation you're in. I hope it stabilizes soon.

Store in fridge and mix well before dosing.

It needs refrigeration to prevent/reduce bacterial growth (which is also the reason for using distilled water).
You don't need to mix it. The cloudiness is from the binder used to keep the tablet in one piece, and bulking agents used to make the tablet large enough to handle. Naltrexone is water soluble so you can just draw the liquid off the top of the container. Some people filter out the binder by using a coffee filter (dampened first so it doesn't absorb much of the naltrexone mixture.)
If starting at 1mg/day is too much then you can use a 50mg tablet in 100ml of water for 0.5mg/day, or 200ml of water for 0.25mg/day depending on your reactions.

I pour some into a container for daily use, keep at room temp. I keep it all at room temp during the winter, refrigerate the larger amount during the summer. I tend to strain out the sediment w/ a cloth.

I store mine in the fridge inside a paper bag, to protect it from light. I'm not sure if that last part is necessary but my mother is a pharmacist and in general she thinks that all drugs should be stored away from light.
Awhile back I had found this study:
http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/9391680

title: Tramadol vs LDN, and long-term side effects of Tramadol

thank you

comments.body: I really don't think you should use both at the same time. LDN won't get you addicted, while opiates like Tramadol (morphine) could. LDN didn't work for me, so now I use Tramadol from time to time.

I think there are no long term effects of LDN. Start slow with a low dose if you experience side effects. As I said opiates like Tramadol can get you addicted in the long run. You will also probably experience some tolerance towards morphine.
It is like comparing apple and oranges - but if you are able to get the necessary pain relief from LDN you should stick to that.
LDN is definitely the better option long term in my opinion.  and yes, some studies  showed LDN increased CD4 t cells in those with HIV so yes it can increase immunity

Is there any speculation about the mechanism of action yet?

From that I guess that it was the opioid response mechanism, but I can't rule out other possibilities, such as antiinflammatory effects restoring normal neural function.

I don't think anyone has figured out the exact mechanism, but LDN may work for ME/CFS because it:
Blocks TLR-4 on microglia
(anti-inflammatory).
Inhibits TLR-9 expression
.
Increases levels of met-enkephalin
(opioid growth factor) and its receptor.
Transiently blocks mu-, delta- and kappa-opioid receptors, which is thought then up-regulates endorphins.
May reduce peroxynitrite
and may thereby increase astrocyte glutamate transport.
Has an effect the
nociceptin
system.
Is a prokinetic
which helps treat SIBO (some ME/CFS patients have worsened symptoms due to comorbid SIBO).

I've been on it for 8 months without any result. (worked up to 4.5mg over a few months)

Hello

I would be very cautious with the interpretation of TLR measurements in studies and how they deduce TLR regulation. TLR activation is a complex topic for the pathophysiology of pathogens because they all use different ways to manipulate receptors for their needs. However, I tend to believe that a normalization of receptor activation is always preferable while the innate immune system allows for a more subtle and differentiated intervention in viral mechanisms. This is also the case for TLR-induced pathways.
I wish there was a simple answer to the TLR-MyD88-NFkB topic, but it's one of the most confusing areas I found for the role of antiviral vs. proviral potency. title: Ultra Low Dose Naltrexone plus opioid for better pain relief
body:
This article
explains how Ultra Low Dose Naltrexone (ULDN) can be used with opioids to improve the pain relief effect provided by the opioids and avoid the increase in pain that is usually associated with long term use.
"Ultra-low-dose naltrexone seems to help block the activation of glial cells caused by long term opioid use, and prevent the amplification of pain that can be induced by long-term opiate use. At very low doses it can do this without blocking the pain-relieving actions of the opiates. The key is finding the dosage sweet spot where LDN is able to calm the glial cells, but not knock the opiates off their receptors. That sweet spot seems to be around 0.5–1mg, called ultra-low-dose naltrexone (usual low-dose naltrexone is 3–4.5mg)."
For those who deal with pain this might be a useful treatment to look into.

• You could try
countering some of the factors that increase microglial activation
. Lipopolysaccharide, interferon gamma and homocysteine all increase microglial activation.
• You could try some of the drugs and supplements that lower
the release of inflammatory cytokines from microglia
.
• You could try some of the drugs and supplements that lower
the release of inflammatory cytokines from astrocytes
. In studies, coxsackievirus B, a virus strongly linked to ME/CFS, has been found to infect astrocytes, and then cause the chronic release of inflammatory cytokines from these infected astrocytes. So perhaps inhibiting the release of inflammatory cytokines from astrocytes might be beneficial.
• You could try some of the drugs and supplements that help switch activated microglia from their
neurodestructive mode
(the "kill mode") to the
neuroprotective mode
(the "heal and repair" mode). Activated microglia do not have to operate in this neurodestructive mode, they can also operate in the neuroprotective mode. Drugs and supplements that help switch activated microglia to the neuroprotective mode include: genistein, sulforaphane and artesunate.

title: Vitamin D may be vital for the efficacy of low-dose naltrexone (LDN)
body:
I just came across the following comment by researcher
Prof Angus G Dalgleish
about how
vitamin D3 (cholecalciferol) is vital
for the clinical efficacy of
low-dose naltrexone
(LDN):
I cannot find any other references for low levels of vitamin D3 making LDN less effective, but for anyone who is thinking of trying LDN, it may be an idea to supplement with say 5,000 to 10,000 IU of vitamin D3 daily for several weeks before starting LDN (and continuing to supplement while taking LDN), to ensure vitamin D levels are adequate.
Note that it takes several weeks of supplementing to slowly build-up blood levels of vitamin D; so you'd probably want to start taking vitamin D first for a few weeks, before starting on LDN.
And for those already benefiting from LDN: it is possible that the addition of vitamin D3 might further improvement the benefits.
Dr Chia
finds
that LDN only helps a small subset of ME/CFS patients, but for those it helps, it does so very significantly. Perhaps if LDN were to be taken in combination with vitamin D3, a higher percentage of ME/CFS patients might respond to it.
The Possible Synergistic Mechanism of Action of LDN and Vitamin D
A possible mechanism of action that might explain why vitamin D is synergistic with LDN is as follows. First, note that LDN has a number of effects that may underlie why it can be helpful for ME/CFS and other diseases:
Low-Dose Naltrexone Physiological Effects
:
Blocks TLR-4 on microglia
, inhibiting microglial activation.
Antagonizes
TLR-9, as well as TLR-7 and TLR-8.
Increases levels of met-enkephalin
(aka opioid growth factor) and its receptor.
Blocks the mu-opioid, delta-opioid and kappa-opioid receptors for a short while (thought to up-regulate endorphins).
Has an effect on the
nociceptin
system.
May reduce peroxynitrite and thereby increase astrocyte glutamate transport. Ref:
1
In the case of LDN's effects on TLR-4, a number of studies have shown that vitamin D down-regulates the expression of TLR-4, so vitamin D may act synergistically with LDN in reducing overall TLR-4 activation, thus inhibiting microglial activation. Refs:
1
2
3
4
5
6
7
Combining Vitamin D With other Immunomodulators Like Oxymatrine
Supplementing with vitamin D might be of benefit with other immunomodulators like oxymatrine. Oxymatrine has also been shown to down-regulate the expression of TLR-4, which in turn reduces microglial activation. Refs:
1
2
3
So adding a vitamin D supplement (or doing lots of sunbathing) to your oxymatrine protocol might further enhance the effects on TLR-4.
Interestingly enough,
@gregh286
found that when he first tried oxymatrine (Equilibrant) it had no effect on his ME/CFS. But when he re-tried oxymatrine later, but this time taking 25,000 IU of vitamin D3 daily, it led to substantial improvements. Ref:
1

"Although the optimal dosage of LDN for the average adult (presumed to weigh 150 pounds) is considered to be 4.5 mg, some patients do much better (i.e., have fewer side effects and a better response) on a lower dose. title: What to do next: LDN or immunovir
body:
Hi
I am trying to decide how to move forward with my treatment. I am managing a lot of my symptoms through various treatments but can't seem to identify a treatment that works for symptoms such as sore throats, swollen glands, virus /flu like feeling. I am in a position where I can either:
1) Pay a private doctor to test for cytokines and specific viruses -parovirus 19, HSV 5/6. (Had most of the other viruses/testing) This particular hospital will provide treatment (immunivor) based on the results. The main disadvantage of this option is I would have to pay out £1000 for testing and then also £75 per month for treatment. I'm also sure I can get another type of anti viral if needs be.
2) just start a prescription of LDN. I can get this online via a private doctor but I don't have anyone to monitor me or speak to in relation to this. A big advantage of this is that it only costs £30 per month and apparently is tolerated well.
I just wanted to ask your advice on what to do as I am really struggling to know what would be best for my symptoms. I've been reading that although LDN is used for pain it can help regulate the immune system.
I also think that maybe the first option actually deals with the potential root of the illness rather just dealing with symptoms.
Your thoughts would be greatly appreciated.
K

comments.body:
I take both.    I've been taking immunovir for over a year, alternating with a different immune modulator.  I can't say that I notice much of a difference with the immunovir, but that could be because I'm pretty sick.    I just started the LDN so I'm not sure about that.
Immunovir is an interferon inducer, I think the LDN is a th1 shifter.
You can get immunovir for about $100/month without an RX.  That's a bit under what you are saying.

You can buy a lot of drugs with £1000.
Do you have any positive or other test results so far? Have you asked to see a NHS Infectious Disease Consultant for testing Parovirus and CMV - I know that they won't do a Cytokines profile and I don't know how good their viral testing is (and they don't do HHV6/7)
My approach was to buy my own drugs on the internet but I have had private testing in the past. If I was to do it again I would buy drugs to try and target the more common infections. I find Antiviral drugs and immunovir helpful but not tried LDN yet.

Both LDN and Imunovir have good safety profiles so I think you could try either (or both) without £1000 of testing.
If you do have HHV6 or CMV, typically Valcyte or cidofovir are needed to lower those titers. Some people have had success with Famvir as well.  You could always pursue this option later with private testing if you do not see enough improvement with the others first.

You can get Immunovir online without a script. LDN too...

Is this because you find LDN loses its effects over time? If so what does your dosing schedule look like? How long do you wait before it starts working again?

Yes.
Originally I took a very long time to go from a starting dose of either 0.5 or 0.75, increasing in 0.25 increments, with the aim of reaching 4.5mg. When I started and every time I increased I got a herx reaction lasting between 5-7 days, during this time I was effectively bed bound - I could move around but I was so ill it was better to just lie there.
So after the 5-7 day period, the herx would stop and I'd be back to normal. Over time I had improvements with LDN to the point where I was able to do a course and a class, and although I was still very ill from doing that I could actually physically get there, which would have been impossible before LDN. I was doing well enough that I was also planning on starting my own business (I still have the all the website sitting on my computer), then the LDN stopped working.
I came off it for a while. I have fiddled around quite a bit since then trying various methods of taking it, and talked to others who had the same kind of experience.
For me, it seems to work best when I feel very ill... Then I take it until I feel a lot better and stop seeing any improvements, and then I stop it until I feel ill enough to need it again.
For example, earlier this year I was pretty much housebound and partially bedbound (was spending about 20 hours a day in bed and only going out for appointments or in a wheelchair), so I started LDN again and took it through until August.
It improved me enough that I'm now partially housebound (I spend more time out of bed in the day and can go out once a week, as well as take my dog out sometimes). I will resume taking it when/if this improvement starts to slide back down again.
I also found I do not need the full 4.5mg dose. I am okay on 1-1.5mg. I take it for 3 weeks, break for 2 or 3 days (miss 2-3 doses), resume taking it and repeat that cycle until I am no longer seeing improvements. The small break is to try to prolong how long I can take it before reaching a plateau of no more improvements.
I should clarify that amongst other health problems, I also have autoimmune thyroid disease (for which I take natural dessicated thyroid). So I am not sure whether the LDN is working primarily on this condition or not... I have had M.E. since 1991 and AI thyroid disease since 2009, and LDN is the only thing that had ever touched my M.E. symptoms.
It's really frustrating isn't it. I hope you can get it to work for you again.

Here are some pointers to consider if LDN isn't working (they seem to cover lack of effect more than fading effect, but maybe there is some information that could help):
When LDN isn't working.
You can try pulsing. Take it every other day, or every couple of days. Or take for a month, stop for a week, take for another month. Or try varying the dose with each pulse (ie. 3mg one day, 4mg the next. Maybe it could prevent the body from adapting to a consistent dose, if adaptation is what is causing loss of effect.) One doctor uses split dosing, 1/2 in the morning, then 1/2 in the evening.

This is exactly what I do. Once a drug passes from a solid to a liquid state, its shelf life can decrease dramatically.  Therefore, do not make more than 50 ml of liquid Naltrexone at one time, store it in the refrigerator, and do not keep it for more than 2 months.
damn i've been keeping my naltrexone in the fridge for like 5 months, should i consider it useless now???

It might not be useless, but it might be contaminated by bacteria etc. One reason for using distilled water, refrigeration, and 1-2 months max storage time is that micro-organisms can grow in the solution. I mix small batches based on a single Naltrexone tablet so that it doesn't sit for long in the fridge.

wow, I thought it would be ok in the fridge, especially since it isn't a solution that has sugar, I thought it wouldn't be that hospitable to bacteria growth.  guess I'll throw it out and use the capsules I have to make volumetric solutions--a little less precise

This Canadian web site seems to still exist, and so I may try to mail order that route.

I have to then cut the pills and dilute myself.
You can bring Pharma pills in your suitcase. I only have ten left.
